title: Fagioli all'Uccelletto
subtitle: Tuscan white beans braised with tomato, garlic, and sage
excerpt: Fagioli all'uccelletto is a Tuscan dish of cannellini beans braised with tomato, garlic, and sage in olive oil. The beans absorb the tomato and become very creamy inside a sauce that is thick and slightly sweet. It works as a side dish, a first course with bread, or a base for grilled sausages.
sourceNotes: Fagioli all'uccelletto is a Florentine standard, found in every trattoria in Tuscany. The name uccelletto means 'little bird' and refers to the seasoning, which is the same used for small game birds in Tuscan cooking: sage, garlic, and olive oil. The recipe appears in Pellegrino Artusi's La Scienza in Cucina (1891) and in nearly every subsequent Tuscan cookbook.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily. Keeps in the fridge for 4 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. Reheat gently over low heat with a splash of water.

content.text: Fagioli all'uccelletto is one of the most straightforward things to cook: tinned cannellini beans braised with tomato, garlic, and sage until thick and creamy. The beans do not need soaking; a good tin works well here. The dish takes about 30 minutes from start to finish and keeps well in the fridge, improving as it sits. Serve it with good bread, grilled sausages, or roast pork.
Warm the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and sage leaves. Cook for 2 minutes until the garlic is lightly golden and the sage begins to crisp.
Add the tinned tomatoes and crush them with a spoon. Season with salt. Cook for 10 minutes over medium heat until the sauce has thickened.

Add the drained beans and stir to coat them in the sauce. Add a small splash of water if the mixture looks dry. Cover and cook over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are very tender and the sauce coats them thickly.
Taste and season with salt and black pepper. Remove the garlic cloves if you prefer a milder flavour, or leave them in. Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and good crusty bread.

Tuscany is the region most linked to bean dishes in Italy. Tuscans are sometimes called 'mangiafagioli' (bean eaters) by other Italians. Fagioli all'uccelletto is the Florentine version, found in trattorias across the city and served alongside grilled meat. The sage and garlic seasoning is the same used for small birds in Tuscan cooking. That is where the name comes from: 'uccelletto' means little bird.
